saints.name: St. Catherine of Alexandria
saints.title: Virgin and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A learned virgin-martyr of the early Church, honoured as a patroness of philosophers and students…
biography: According to her ancient and beloved passion, Catherine was a noblewoman of Alexandria of singular learning, born late in the third century. Converted to Christ as a young woman, she rebuked the Emperor Maxentius for persecuting the Church, whereupon he summoned fifty of the empire's best philosophers to refute her; she confuted them, and they, converted, were put to death.

Imprisoned and scourged, she converted the empress herself and the officer set to guard her. Condemned to die upon a spiked wheel, she saw it shattered at her prayer, and was at last beheaded, about the year 305; legend holds that angels bore her body to Mount Sinai.

Her relics are venerated to this day in the monastery on Sinai built by the Emperor Justinian, which bears her name, and her cult, carried west by returning crusaders, made her one of the most beloved saints of the Middle Ages and one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.

Her feast, removed from the general calendar in 1969, was restored in 2002. Because she overcame the learned in debate, she is a patroness of philosophers and students; because of the wheel of her passion, of wheelwrights and all who work with wheels.
saints.knownFor: Confounding pagan philosophers and dying for the faith.
